desc:
Among all non-empty strictly increasing subsequences of nums, find the one whose elements add up to the largest total, and return that total.

A subsequence keeps the original order of the chosen elements. It may have length 1. Values can be negative, so a longer subsequence is not always better. For nums = [1, 101, 2, 3, 100, 4, 5] the answer is 106 (1 + 2 + 3 + 100).
hints: Instead of the length, let total[i] be the best sum of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends exactly at index i.
total[i] = nums[i] + the best total[j] among earlier j with nums[j] < nums[i]; but if every such total[j] is negative (or there is no j), start fresh and use nums[i] alone.
The answer is the maximum total[i] over all i. A Fenwick tree (prefix maximum over value ranks) speeds the O(n<sup>2</sup>) double loop up to O(n log n).
editorial: This is the longest increasing subsequence recurrence with a different quantity: instead of counting elements, add them. Let total[i] be the maximum sum of a strictly increasing subsequence whose last element is nums[i]. Then total[i] = nums[i] + max(0, max total[j]) over indices j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]. The max(0, ...) handles both the case with no valid predecessor and the case where every predecessor sum is negative and extending would hurt.

The answer is the largest total[i]; it must be taken over all i because the best subsequence can end anywhere. The two nested loops cost O(n2) time. To reach O(n log n), compress the values to ranks and keep a Fenwick tree that answers 'maximum total among values with rank below r' and supports point updates that keep the maximum.
solution:
from bisect import bisect_left

def maxSumIncreasing(nums):
    vals = sorted(set(nums))
    m = len(vals)
    NEG = -10 ** 18
    tree = [NEG] * (m + 1)
    best = NEG
    for x in nums:
        k = bisect_left(vals, x)          # ranks 1..k hold values smaller than x
        q = NEG
        i = k
        while i > 0:
            if tree[i] > q:
                q = tree[i]
            i -= i & -i
        cur = x + (q if q > 0 else 0)
        i = k + 1
        while i <= m:
            if tree[i] < cur:
                tree[i] = cur
            i += i & -i
        if cur > best:
            best = cur
    return best
